title: ALLNET own line
desc: Own-brand switches, racks, cabling and more

pages.t: ALLNET GmbH Computersysteme describes itself as a developer and manufacturer of modern network and communication technology. It is based in Germering near Munich and says many products are developed in its own labs.
g: A company that designs products itself, not only resells other companies' products.
A company's own label, sold next to or instead of other makers' brands. German: Hausmarke.

pages.t: ALLNET presents ALLNET Brand as its house brand. Its main areas are networking, digital signage, video surveillance and building automation. For you the most important part is networking: switches, racks, media converters, PoE and wireless.
g: Screens that show changing content such as menus, ads or information in shops and lobbies.
Controlling lights, heating, sensors and sockets in a building over the network.

pages.t: Allnet Nordic describes itself as part of the Allnet group and acts as distributor. Your customers are resellers and installers, who sell to companies, schools and hotels. A reseller who knows the ALLNET Brand can say what it covers and where it fits.
g: A company that buys from the maker and sells to resellers, not to end users.
A company that sells IT products and services on to end customers.

quiz.q: How does ALLNET GmbH describe itself?
o: A pure online retailer of consumer gadgets
A developer and manufacturer of network and communication technology
A telecom operator selling mobile contracts
quiz.w: ALLNET calls itself a developer and manufacturer of modern network and communication technology, with many products developed in its own labs.

quiz.q: What is the ALLNET Brand?
o: ALLNET's house brand (Hausmarke) with networking as one main area
A certification given to other vendors
The name of a fibre standard
quiz.w: ALLNET Brand is ALLNET's own house brand. Networking is one of its main areas, next to signage, video surveillance and building automation.

quiz.q: Who is Allnet Nordic's customer in this setup?
quiz.w: A distributor supplies resellers and installers, who then serve the end customer.

lessons.title: The range and the Synergy 21 label

pages.t: The product tree is wide: 19 inch cabinets and racks, switches, PoE products, media converters and SFP modules, WLAN, xDSL modems and routers, Powerline, UPS and power supplies, video cameras, serial device servers and sensors for IP building automation.
g: A small plug-in module that gives a switch a fibre or copper port.
Battery backup that keeps equipment running during a power cut.

pages.t: ALLNET's shop and catalogue sell structured cabling: patch cables, patch panels and keystone modules. These carry the Synergy 21 label, a separate cable label sold through ALLNET, not the ALLNET Brand name itself. Be exact when you speak to customers.
g: The organised, permanent cabling of a building: wall sockets, patch panels and cables.
A small snap-in socket module that fits into patch panels and wall plates.

pages.t: Cabinets, base frames and wall housings are listed under ALLNET Brand and carry the ALLNET name. In the older catalogue the same book also lists patch panels, patch cables, fibre patch cables and power strips, so one supplier can cover a whole network room.
g: A rack-mounted board of sockets where building cables end and short patch cables connect to switches.

quiz.q: Which label do ALLNET's copper patch cables in the shop carry?
quiz.w: The patch cable listing in ALLNET's shop shows Synergy 21 as the only brand.

quiz.q: Which of these is listed under the ALLNET Brand product tree?
quiz.w: The tree includes 19 inch cabinets and racks, switches, media converters, WLAN, Powerline, UPS, video surveillance and more.

quiz.q: A customer asks for 'the ALLNET patch cable'. What is the most accurate reply?
o: There is no cabling in the group at all
The cables are sold through ALLNET under the Synergy 21 label
quiz.w: Be exact: ALLNET's shop sells the cables under the separate Synergy 21 label.

quiz.q: Why does a wide range matter to an installer?
o: It lets him buy racks, switches and cabling for one project from one supplier
It removes the need for planning
quiz.w: One supplier for cabinet, switch and cabling simplifies ordering and support. It says nothing about price.

pages.t: The SoHo Line covers unmanaged and smart managed Layer 2 switches. Example: ALL-SG8245PM, five gigabit ports, four with PoE, fanless and set up from a web page. Suits small offices and workplaces with printers, PCs and access points.
g: Cooled without a fan, so silent and one less part to fail.
Basic switching of traffic between devices on the same network.

pages.t: Professional Line comes in two flavours: smart managed 19 inch rack switches, and Layer2+ full managed switches. Example: ALL-SG9312M-10G with 12 SFP+ 10G ports, web and command-line management, aimed at medium or large networks as a core switch.
g: The central switch that all other switches connect to.
The 10 gigabit version of an SFP slot.

pages.t: ALLNET also lists industrial switches, outdoor switches, PD switches that are powered through PoE themselves, and a switch for smart home use in the electrical cabinet. On the page ALLNET gives a 24 month warranty for its switches.
g: A switch that receives its power over a PoE cable instead of a power plug.

quiz.q: Which line fits a small office with a few PCs, a printer and one access point?
o: Professional Line core switch with 12 SFP+ ports
quiz.w: The SoHo Line is meant for small offices and workplaces. A 10G core switch would be oversized.

quiz.q: What is ALL-SG9312M-10G?
o: A 12-port SFP+ 10G rackmount switch for larger networks
quiz.w: It is in the Professional Line smart managed rackmount category, with twelve 10G SFP+ ports.

quiz.q: What is a PD switch?
o: A switch that is powered over PoE
quiz.w: PD means powered device: the switch gets its power from a PoE cable.
g: Power over Ethernet: power and data in one network cable.

pages.t: ALLNET lists 19 inch standing cabinets in 12, 22, 32 and 42 U, plus base frames (open racks without doors). In the catalogue the SNB cabinets are lockable, come with fans and a thermostat, and have cable entries at top and bottom.
g: The standard width for rack equipment: 19 inches between the mounting rails.
An open rack frame with no doors or side panels.

pages.t: Wall housings run from small 10 inch cases of up to 9 U up to 19 inch housings of 3 to 27 U. The small 10 inch case in the catalogue is a welded steel case with a lockable glass door and passive ventilation slits.
g: Height unit in a rack. One U is 44.45 mm. A 12 U cabinet holds twelve units of equipment.

pages.t: SNB cabinets exist with glass doors or perforated doors. The catalogue says the perforated type gives clearly better airflow. Accessories include shelves, cable guide plates, blank panels, fan units, power strips and drawers.
g: Full of small holes so air can pass through.

quiz.q: Which size range do ALLNET standing cabinets cover in the product list?
quiz.w: Standing cabinets are listed in 12, 22, 32 and 42 U.

quiz.q: The catalogue says one SNB door type gives clearly better air flow. Which?
quiz.w: Perforated sheet doors let air pass through, which helps cooling.

quiz.q: A shop wants a very small box for one switch and a patch panel on the wall. What fits best?
quiz.w: The 10 inch wall housing is a small case of up to 9 U, meant for small wall installations.

lessons.title: Cabling products in the group range

pages.t: The shop lists RJ45 patch cables under Synergy 21 in CAT6 and CAT6A. Examples: round slimline U/FTP cables, flat TPE Superflex cables, and in the old catalogue cables with a lock and key. Many lengths and colours exist.
g: The standard plug on network cables.
A thinner cable, easier to route in crowded racks.

pages.t: The catalogue lists 19 inch patch panels with 16 or 24 ports in CAT6 and CAT6A, keystone panels, half-height 0.5 U panels, surface-mount wall boxes and RJ45 wall sockets. This is the fixed part of a network, between the cable in the wall and the switch.
g: A 0.5 U panel, useful where rack space is tight.

pages.t: The shop has a fibre category called Verkabelung LWL, and the catalogue lists fibre patch cables and fibre patch panels. It also lists cable testers. Check the live shop for what is in stock, as ranges and availability change.

quiz.q: Which patch panel sizes does the catalogue list for CAT6 and CAT6A?
quiz.w: The catalogue lists 16 and 24 port panels, plus keystone and half-height versions.

quiz.q: What does slimline mean for a patch cable?
o: It is thinner and easier to route
quiz.w: Slimline cables are thin and round, which helps in dense racks.

quiz.q: What is a keystone panel?
o: A panel where each port is a snap-in module
quiz.w: Keystone modules snap into a carrier, so you choose the socket type per port.

pages.t: Each category supports a higher frequency: Cat5e 100 MHz, Cat6 up to 250 MHz, Cat6A 500 MHz, Cat7 600 MHz, Cat8 2000 MHz. More frequency means room for faster Ethernet. The maximum length of a normal link is 100 m.
g: Megahertz, how fast the signal in the cable swings. Higher means more capacity.
A grade for twisted-pair cable. A higher number is a higher grade.

pages.t: Both run gigabit over 100 m. Cat6 can carry 10 gigabit only to about 55 m, while Cat6A reaches the full 100 m at 10 gigabit. Cat6A is usually the choice for new buildings and backbone runs. Cat5e is fine for simple gigabit.
g: 10 gigabit Ethernet over twisted pair copper.

pages.t: Cat7 is not recognised by TIA, and it is often sold with ordinary RJ45 plugs. Cat8 supports 25 and 40 gigabit but only up to 30 m (TIA), so it is a data room short-link product. Most office jobs are served by Cat6A.
g: Telecommunications Industry Association, a US body that writes cabling standards.

quiz.q: A new office building needs 10 gigabit copper runs of 80 m. Which is the standard choice?
quiz.w: Cat6A is specified for 10 gigabit over the full 100 m. Cat6 only reaches about 55 m at 10 gigabit.

quiz.q: What is the typical maximum length of a standard copper Ethernet link?
quiz.w: 100 m is the normal limit for gigabit over twisted pair.

quiz.q: Where does Cat8 make sense?
o: Long runs of 100 m in offices
Short links of up to 30 m in data rooms
quiz.w: Cat8 supports 25 and 40 gigabit but only on short links, TIA specifies up to 30 m.

quiz.q: What is true about Cat7?
o: It is the official TIA successor of Cat6A
quiz.w: Cat7 comes from the ISO world. TIA does not recognise it, and it is often fitted with RJ45 plugs.

src.l: Cables and Kits: PVC vs LSZH jackets

pages.t: The first letter is the shield around the whole cable, the second the shield around each pair. U is none, F is foil, S is braid. So U/UTP has no shield, F/UTP has foil overall, S/FTP has braid overall plus foil per pair.
g: A metal layer that keeps outside electrical noise out of the signal.
A woven mesh of thin copper wires.

pages.t: LSZH jackets give little smoke and no halogens in a fire, so less toxic and corrosive gas. They are used where people or poor ventilation matter, for example tunnels or ships. PVC is the common standard jacket and gives off more smoke and corrosive gas when it burns.
g: Low smoke, zero halogen: a cable jacket that gives off little smoke and no halogen gases when burning.

pages.t: Solid cable has one thick wire per conductor and is for permanent runs in walls. Stranded cable is many fine wires, flexible, and used for patch cords. Mixing them up can give unreliable connections.
g: A short, flexible cable between a socket or panel and a device.

quiz.q: What does S/FTP mean?
o: Braid over the whole cable and foil on each pair
Foil over the whole cable only
quiz.w: S is braid for the overall shield, F is foil on each pair.

quiz.q: Which cable goes inside the wall for a permanent link?
quiz.w: Solid core is for permanent installation. Stranded cable is for flexible patch cords.

quiz.q: Why would a customer ask for LSZH?
o: Fire safety: little smoke and no halogen gas
quiz.w: LSZH jackets limit smoke and toxic gas in a fire. They do not change the speed.

quiz.q: What is the first letter in F/UTP about?
quiz.w: The first letter is the overall shield: here foil. The pairs themselves are unshielded.

pages.t: Multimode fibre has a wide core where light takes many paths. It suits buildings and campuses; OM3 carries 10 gigabit to about 300 m. Single-mode has one light path and goes much further, for example between sites.
g: Grades of multimode fibre, often with aqua jackets.
Fibre with a thin core and one light path, for long distances.

pages.t: An SFP is a small plug-in module that decides what fibre a port takes. ALLNET lists SFP modules, for example an industrial single-mode LC module for up to 10 km at 100 Mbit, rated for -40 to +85 degrees. Modules often come separately from the switch.
g: A small fibre connector, common on SFP modules.

pages.t: A media converter links copper and fibre. ALLNET lists gigabit models from copper to an SFP slot, including one with a built-in PoE injector. Use it when a fibre run meets a device that only has an RJ45 port.
g: A device that adds power to a network cable for a PoE device.

quiz.q: Two buildings on a campus are 10 km apart. Which fibre type?
quiz.w: Single-mode goes much further than multimode. Copper is limited to 100 m.

quiz.q: What is an SFP?
o: A plug-in module that gives a switch port its fibre or copper type
quiz.w: SFP modules are plugged into switches and converters to choose the link type.

quiz.q: A fibre line ends at an IP camera that only has RJ45 and needs power. What helps?
o: A media converter with a PoE injector
quiz.w: A media converter links fibre to copper, and the model with a PoE injector also supplies power.

lessons.title: Choosing a switch: managed, PoE, uplinks

pages.t: Unmanaged switches are plug and play and cannot create VLANs. Smart managed adds a web page with basic settings. Managed gives full control and monitoring but needs skilled staff. Choose by what the customer must separate or monitor.
g: A way to split one physical network into separate virtual ones, for example guests and staff.

pages.t: PoE standards differ: about 13 W at the device for 802.3af, 25 W for 802.3at, up to 51 or 71 W for 802.3bt. A switch has a total budget: ALL-SG8245PM has four PoE ports up to 30 W each, but only about 50 to 60 W in total (the vendor page gives both figures).
g: The total power a switch can hand out over all its PoE ports together.

pages.t: Add up the devices first: cameras, phones, access points. Then check PoE watts and port count. For links between switches, pick a model with SFP slots so fibre can be used. Industrial and core models show SFP slots clearly.
g: The link from one switch to the next switch or core.

quiz.q: A hotel wants guests and staff on separate virtual networks. What do you need?
o: A smart managed or managed switch with VLAN support
quiz.w: Unmanaged switches cannot create VLANs. Smart managed or managed switches can.

quiz.q: A switch has four PoE ports at 30 W each and a total budget of about 60 W. What does that mean?
o: All four ports can deliver 30 W at once
The ports share the 60 W total
quiz.w: The budget is the total. Four devices at 30 W would need 120 W.

quiz.q: Which gives the most control but needs skilled staff?
quiz.w: Fully managed switches give full control and monitoring but need experienced administrators.

quiz.q: Which standard gives the most power at the device?
quiz.w: 802.3bt gives up to 51 or 71 W at the device, af about 13 W, at about 25 W.

src.l: Cables and Kits: server rack guide

pages.t: Add the height of every device in U, then add spare. Count switches, patch panels, shelves and the UPS. A 42 U cabinet is one of the most common full heights. Leave room for growth: a full cabinet is a problem the day you add one switch.
g: One rack unit is 44.45 mm of height.

pages.t: Depth has no standard: racks often come in 600, 800 or about 1000 mm. Servers and long switches need depth, and cables need room behind them. ALLNET's 800 mm wide cabinets in the catalogue have side cable ducts, which keeps larger installations tidy.
g: A channel that guides cables vertically inside a cabinet.

pages.t: Equipment mostly takes air in at the front and blows it out the back, so a closed cabinet needs fans or perforated doors. Small jobs use a wall housing, larger ones a floor cabinet. A wall housing has a weight limit: the 10 inch ALLNET case takes up to 30 kg.
g: Cool air enters the front of equipment and warm air leaves at the back.

quiz.q: Which is the most common full height of a cabinet?
quiz.w: 42 U is one of the most common full cabinet heights.

quiz.q: Why would an installer choose a deeper cabinet?
o: For servers, long devices and cable room
quiz.w: Depth is not standardised. Servers and cables need space behind the front rails.

quiz.q: A closed cabinet will hold a heating switch stack. What helps?
quiz.w: Airflow is key: fans in the cabinet or perforated doors help heat escape.

pages.t: A small office: SoHo smart managed PoE switch, Cat6 patch cables, 10 inch or small wall housing. A school: managed rack switches with VLANs for staff, pupils and guests, Cat6A in the walls and a 22 or 32 U cabinet. This is a judgement, not an ALLNET rule.
g: A separate network for visitors that cannot reach internal systems.

pages.t: A hotel needs PoE for access points, VLANs to separate guests and back office, and often fibre between floors. A data room needs a standing cabinet with airflow, SFP+ uplinks such as the ALL-SG9312M-10G, and tidy cable ducts.
g: Internal systems such as reception and booking, kept apart from guests.

pages.t: Factories need DIN rail switches with wide temperature range. ALL-SGI8016PM is managed, fanless, -40 to +75 degrees, with 12 PoE ports and SFP uplinks. ALL-SGI8104v3 is the unmanaged option, 4 copper ports and 2 SFP slots.
g: A standard metal rail inside control cabinets that devices clip onto.

quiz.q: A factory wants a switch for a control cabinet with wide temperature range. Which fits?
o: Industrial DIN rail switch such as ALL-SGI8016PM
quiz.w: ALL-SGI8016PM is a fanless DIN rail switch rated -40 to +75 degrees.

quiz.q: A school wants staff, pupils and guests on separate networks. What is needed?
quiz.w: VLAN support requires a smart managed or managed switch.

quiz.q: A data room needs 10 gigabit links between racks. Which fits?
o: A switch with SFP+ ports such as ALL-SG9312M-10G
quiz.w: ALL-SG9312M-10G has twelve 10G SFP+ ports and is aimed at larger networks.

quiz.q: A small office has four PoE devices. What is the first check?
quiz.w: Add up device watts and compare to the switch total budget.

pages.t: Some cheap cable uses CCA, copper-clad aluminium. It has roughly 55 percent higher resistance, is more brittle, and cannot carry a Cat rating under TIA or ISO. With PoE it can give too little power. The article finds no widely reported fires.
g: Copper-clad aluminium: an aluminium wire with a thin copper coat.

pages.t: Do not claim danger you cannot prove. Say: standards require copper, CCA fails them, and a failing link costs the installer a call-out. Ask to check jacket markings. Cabling stays in the walls for years.
g: A visit to fix a fault, usually at the installer's cost.

pages.t: Ask: how many devices, and how many PoE watts needed? Which speed in 5 years? Distances over 100 m? Shielded or fire-safe (LSZH) needed? Wall or floor rack? Room for spare U? Managed features? Good questions beat product lists.
g: Empty rack space kept free for future equipment.

quiz.q: A customer offers a cheap cable that might be CCA. What is the best response?
o: Say it will start a fire
Explain that standards require copper and ask to check the markings
quiz.w: Stay factual: CCA does not meet the standards, and PoE can suffer, but fires are not widely reported.

quiz.q: Which question helps choose a switch?
o: How many PoE watts do the devices need?
quiz.w: PoE watts decide whether the budget is enough.

quiz.q: Why ask about LSZH?
o: Fire safety needs in the building
quiz.w: LSZH reduces smoke and halogen gas in a fire, it does not change speed.
